transcript: The other night I attended a production of Unclevania staged at a loft apartment in Manhattan near Union Square. This production was extremely intimate, with the actors being surrounded on all 4 sides by audience members sitting on chairs and bar stools, which I thought were unfortunately very uncomfortable. I wasn't familiar with Unclevania before seeing this production, but it's more or less a slow burning family drama where people are miserable and make each other miserable. The tension between characters was palpable, especially given the intimate nature of this production. I thought the acting was overall phenomenal and the relationships between characters felt super genuine. This production generally felt pretty modern, but the translation was a bit clunky to me, and there were some moments in the dialogue that made the characters feel unrelatable by the way that they were speaking. But otherwise I thought it was really, really great and the 2 and 1/2 hours honestly flew by with how present I felt in the room. The acting, direction and design of this production made for a series of gripping moments, both big and small. With that, another program for my collection.
